Replay

Replay Scrapyard — canonical editor-first example

8 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Run nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/play.sh from the repository root, then choose Solo to try the game. Scrapyard calls its player characters runners and its guns irons. Replay's runtime runner is separate: it schedules simulation steps and manages input/history. Godot presents the resulting state and effects through authored scenes.

The visual contributor guide starts with running the game, then follows a turret from input to scene. Use it to choose a first change and identify the tests that cover it.

The code guide maps the frame loop, input, session startup, event handling and presentation, with the project's formatting command.

Shared turret adds a deployable ability that any player can operate, with shared ammunition, predicted claims, handoffs and occupied recovery.

Stormcaller demonstrates a Replay-only enemy with an authored pulse attack, a composed charge view, and tested correction/recovery behavior.

The editor workflow adds validation/baking, refreshable previews, Resource pickers, feature drafts and an ability workbench with replay tests.

The authoring tools workflow covers typed enemy registration, one canonical bake, frozen revisions and reusable feature tests.

For scene composition, read the editor-first authoring guide. It explains authored actor scenes, reusable child components, detached HUD/display values, and validated gameplay Resources around the replayable model. Enemy, runner, and HUD scenes have independent F6 previews. The initial bridge comparison retains the earlier integration's measured tradeoffs; use the authoring guide for current composition.

Dash input uses receipt-time actions with explicit outcomes; movement and held combat input retain scheduled controls.

The online party menu creates, joins and rejoins rooms through the standalone Replay room service. It uses the shared Party helper while keeping personal progression separate from network credentials and retaining asset-aware takeover checks. Native TLS and local browser RTC gates pass; the full port and public deployment remain in progress.

This separate Replay implementation keeps the sibling Scrapyard game runnable. It covers seeded cover, runner movement/dash, staging, ballistics, grenades, historical rail/healing queries, all enemy brains, status/reaction rules, damage, drops, camera, and multiplayer views. The historical port ledger records remaining comparison work. This authoring example does not establish exhaustive parity with the original game.

Audio and local settings include the original sound assets, music crossfades, persisted volume/shake preferences and menu controls.

Original dirt/grass dressing and the animated gate/direction arrow are restored. The scenery gate checks three floors across host/client/observer. The bottom shop cards provide clickable purchases in the original shortcut order; broader HUD and hardware-audio parity remain work.

The combat HUD includes the original health/cooldown/status displays, large magazine, boss health and revive prompt, driven from Replay state.

Run transitions include large departure/wipe panels, current wave/rest information and recovery narration reconstructed from state.

Borrowed eyes follows a living teammate while downed, returns on revival and handles a watched host's loss without changing local controls or HUD.

Chat and yard history include named messages, a late-join scrollback, wave/run announcements and history retained through asset-aware host migration.

Positional pings use middle mouse, with a stamped floating name and the original fading diamond; late-join history excludes old markers.

Browser UI acceptance exercises chat, pings, shop, HUD and camera/revival in three actual Chrome processes with shared world-state checks.

Actor presentation provides downed poses/beacons, muzzle/reload cues, ghost tint and enemy attack/hit/death behavior with lifecycle checks.

Combat feedback adds bounded bursts, debris, damage numbers and pickup effects, with expiry, floor-change and recovery checks.

Screen effects restore the health vignette, zoom kicks and floor veil, with camera-motion controls and native/browser checks.

Directional wounds use recorded hit origins and historical victim positions, with personal-view and expiry checks.

Wall contacts preserve the resolved cover face for ballistic/spit sparks and sound, with bounded capacity and explicit older-save conversion.

Rail and grenade presentation adds beam contact sparks, original shell shapes and bounded ember trails.

Escape menu and tally add screen dimming, responsive panels, healing credit, keyboard focus handling and native/browser Quit.

Staging muster restores player previews, readiness lamps, bidirectional pickers, host Start and late Drop In.

Automatic loadouts persist local choice modes and resolve them for the current seat while keeping gameplay profiles concrete.

Editor workbench provides inspector-driven previews of the real game, with a live tally and Esc menu.

Browser play and migration have a three-browser gate, including PNG upload, an asset-dependent checkpoint, planned/crash recovery and continued combat with whole-world state comparison.

The menu offers Solo, Host, Join, Watch, and Resume solo, using localhost and port 49610 by default. Pick a name, skin, and iron, then mark ready. The displayed lobby leader starts the game. WASD moves, Shift dashes, and holding the left mouse button fires. All seven irons have magazines, automatic reloads and deterministic jams (continued trigger pulls clear jams). The lobber bounces and blasts mobs; the lance pierces; the mender heals the first living friend. Interactive play runs waves, floor clears, shops, regroup/departure and wipe/reset. Hold F to revive; the clear-stage panel lists purchases and parts. Run rules explain what persists within the world. Local co-op profiles save cores, parts and loadouts; Room recovery carries live combat checkpoints to a successor. F5 saves an uncoordinated solo/host run; run saves describe fresh-process resume and identity requirements. RSY_RUN=0 retains isolated encounters; then RSY_ENCOUNTER=mixed, boss or barrels selects those fixtures. Select two abilities in staging, then Q/E cast toward the mouse. Q carries a point; E a direction. Cooldowns appear below the status line. Equip shared turret to deploy one; press T nearby to mount/release, then aim/fire normally. Its last round despawns it and automatically dismounts the operator. Project name, custom user-data directory and port are separate from the original.

The reducer applies input to gameplay values: roster/profile actions, readiness, start/drop-in, movement, dash, gun mechanisms, enemies, projectiles, drops, and events. The server computes accepted state, the local player predicts, and remote characters display on the observed view clock. This differs from the original's owner-streamed movement. The model never calls Godot. Arena rendering and collision use the same saved cover list; camera movement, animation, and smoothing do not modify it.

The test compiles selected unmodified original arena/movement procedures into an isolated oracle and compares every cover plus final position bits for 12 layouts and 48 movement traces. It never runs the original run.sh or clears its profiles. The cached baseline corpus permits standalone tests when the sibling is absent; REPLAY_REQUIRE_BASELINE=1 requires a live source comparison. Native tests also cover staging gates, collision forgiveness, UTF-8 names, rewind and mid-dash checkpoint resume. The gun oracle compares the original magazine/reload/jam mechanism over 16 scenarios; additional combat tests cover occlusion, capacity/conservation, rollback of kills/pickups and active-combat checkpoint continuation. The three-process arena gate checks seed/loadout agreement, movement, one dash per player, effect counts and settled position convergence under latency/faults. The combat gate drives two shooters and a spectator, requires four kills, exactly 29 damage/12 scrap and reconciled shot effects, then compares the complete world at a common authoritative tick. weapon_run.sh also checks grenade/lance combat and a separate wounded-teammate healing scenario, including validated historical queries. RSY_JITTER, RSY_LOSS and RSY_DUPLICATE apply to these gates too.

See combat rules and limits, asset hashes and the port ledger for unmatched rules and missing slices. The current fixed-tick dash is ten ticks, compared with the original's 0.16-second owner-frame duration; variable-frame feel and network trust are not yet matched.

The original ability gate uses three players and a late spectator to exercise the six original abilities: slime lob, igniter cone, frostwave nova, battlecry buff, salvefield zone and sparkjar lob. It checks cross-player reactions, attribution, pulse/expiry behavior and a complete same-tick world comparison. See ability rules for the saved-state contract and remaining comparison limits.

storm_run.sh gives slime/frost to one runner and spark/ignite to another. It proves cross-player freeze/shatter credit, observes burn before dousing, then checks shock spread. A support runner supplies rally/salve and every participant must observe surge. The normal ability gate now explicitly checks that friendly transmutation too.

gauntlet_run.sh exercises all three floor-one waves (4/4/5 enemies), records each saved rest deadline and refuses early wave/floor completion. Its players use normal weapons and support casts, then gather the crew for a separately spawned barrel chain. The matched solo comparison uses isolated original/Replay games with one player and no support casts. All six games clear the waves; one Replay stationary barrel finale is blocked by cover, so the full paired cohort does not pass. Difficulty and human feel remain unverified.

Spray images use content-addressed transfer and value-owned placements. Choose a PNG in staging, then press G to stamp it. The existing decal follows image replacement, and Room preparation waits for referenced image bytes.

Host-owned JSON mods overlay the value catalog in filename order. Clients use the host’s catalog, including sparse loadouts, and saves retain that catalog.

The stress/profiling record includes a 40-enemy workload, raw timings and memory/traffic observations. The optimized-build copy fix permits ordinary -o:speed builds. That stress record did not establish a matched baseline comparison. Later optimized paired idle and firing/reload comparisons passed; the port ledger links those results and their workloads.

Authority-only rewind history reduces ordinary snapshot traffic while preserving complete recovery checkpoints.

The cover-aware solo comparison now verifies blocked shots and ordinary movement around cover through complete wave/barrel finales in both games.

With RSY_DEV=1, the Escape menu includes Export recording. It saves recent authority/prediction frames, controls, actions and verdicts to a native file (RSY_RECORDING_PATH, default user://scrapyard.rplrec) or browser download. The network recording guide explains the headless verifier, compatibility and cost. This diagnostic does not pause the live session or replace its recovery checkpoint.

Dedicated authorities can run with RSY_ROLE=server. The server-act comparison checks two clients through combat and floor progression. For coordinator-managed avatarless authorities, see the Room infrastructure profile.
